        - heading "Understand Normal Line" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A normal line is perpendicular to the tangent line at a point on a curve. In Normal Line, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Normal slope: m_normal=-1/m_tangent. You can learn Normal Line by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Find the tangent slope. Take its negative reciprocal. Use the point on the curve. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, optics: Normals help describe reflection. Watch out: Using tangent slope as normal slope. Normal is perpendicular to tangent."

      - article:
        - heading "Observe" [level=3]
        - paragraph: A tangent touches the curve at point P(x,y). The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent at P.
      - article:
        - heading "Manipulate" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Drag x or h to move P along the curve. Both lines and equations update instantly.
      - article:
        - heading "Notice" [level=3]
        - paragraph: The slope of the normal line is always the negative reciprocal of the tangent slope.
      - article:
        - heading "Understand" [level=3]
        - paragraph: This guarantees the normal line is perpendicular to the tangent at the same selected point.
      - heading "Normal Line – graph + CAS" [level=3]
      - strong: f(x) = −2x² + x
      - generic: Live⌁
      - main:
        - paragraph: Curve f(x)=−2x²+x
        - paragraph: Tangent line (slope m)
        - paragraph: Normal line (slope mₙ)
        - generic: ⓘ The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent at the same selected point.

      - article:
        - heading "Key Rule" [level=3]:
          - text: Key Rule
        - paragraph: "If the tangent slope at P is m (with m finite), then the normal slope mₙ is:"
        - status: mₙ = −1/m
        - paragraph: Valid for all points where m exists and m ≠ 0. For m=0, the normal is vertical.
      - article:
        - heading "Why it works" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Perpendicular lines satisfy m₁ × m₂ = −1. So the normal slope is the negative reciprocal of the tangent slope.
        - status: m × mₙ = −1 ⇒ mₙ = −1/m
      - article:
        - heading "Common Mistake" [level=3]:
          - text: Common Mistake
        - paragraph: Don’t use mₙ = −m. That only makes the lines parallel with opposite direction, not perpendicular.
      - article:
        - heading "⚙ Worked Example" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find the equation of the normal line to y=−2x²+x at x=1.
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "1"
          - text: f(x)=−2x²+x
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "2"
          - text: f′(x)=−4x+1 ⇒ m=f′(1)=−3
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "3"
          - text: mₙ=−1/m=1/3
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "4"
          - text: "Point: P(1,f(1))=(1,−1)"
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "5"
          - text: "Equation: y−(−1)=⅓(x−1)"
        - paragraph:
          - generic: "6"
          - text: y=⅓x−4/3
